content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3 (overtime-backed recovery): the only option that reaches the 80% target, at an extra cost of ₹5,496","why":"Payments calls have run 21-44% above forecast since 11:00 (824 calls vs 634.5 forecast over the last 8 intervals), and service level fell to 15.4% at 12:45. The rise is spread evenly across all call reasons and has no clear cause, so we should plan for it to continue. P3 offers overtime to 18 payments agents 13:30-15:30 and 5 agents 19:00-20:00. It adds chat deflection, delayed breaks and a move of 4 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 15:00-16:00. For the disruption window (13:00-19:15) it predicts 86.1% service level: payments 83.8% and general 90.5%. Predicted abandons are 3.0% and rest of day is 85.7%. There are no policy violations.","trade_offs":["Cost: P3 adds ₹5,496. P2 costs ₹1,266 but reaches only 76.6% (payments 71.2%), missing the 80% target. P1 and no action cost nothing but predict 72.7% and 73.6%.","Customer impact: predicted abandons are 3.0% under P3, against 5.6% (P2), 6.5% (P1) and 7.4% (no action).","General queue: moving 4 agents does not hurt general under P3, which is predicted at 90.5% against 89.5% with no action. P1 and P2 do pull general down slightly, to 87.6% and 86.9%.","Risk: the plan relies on enough agents accepting the overtime offers. If too few accept, results will fall toward P2's level."],"watch":"Track overtime acceptance before 13:30 and payments call volume against forecast each interval. If volume keeps rising past the +44% peak, or acceptance is low, reassess and consider involving the duty manager."}
